Parents
Welcome to our Parents' Area.
This area is designed to keep you up to date with, and give you access to, key information. We will upload our weekly newsletters here along with other letters too, so you won't miss out on any important school information!
Our aim is to work in partnership with all our parents and children to ensure that we continue to offer the best opportunities, education and positive experience of school. This area is designed for you, so if we can add anything to further improve our website to help you, please get in touch and let us know.

pageCache.pageTitle: The School Day - Ibstone Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
The School Day
8.45am – 3.15pm (EYFS & KS1)
8.45am – 3.25pm (KS2) KS2 pupils finish at 3.15pmon Fridays
There is a member of staff on Rolling Drop Off duty from 8.35am. Where possible, please use our Rolling Drop Off system. For children in KS1 upwards, if you are walking the children into school, please park on the road down towards the church, children should be dropped at the school gate. The register is taken at 8.45am and lessons start straight away so it is really important to be at school on time.
All children are invited to make use of the rolling drop off system that runs from 8.35am every morning. The rolling drop off zone is immediately in front of the school and there will be a parent or member of staff waiting to help your child get out of the car. Please make sure your child is sitting on the passenger side of the car so that they can get out safely.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Uniform - Ibstone Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Uniform
School uniform is worn everyday (apart from occasional mufti days). Our EYFS and KS1 children (4-7year olds) and KS2 children (7-11 year olds) have slightly different uniform. These can be seen below:
EYFS and Key Stage 1 Uniform
Key Stage 2 Uniform
Everything you will need can be ordered online from Sportscrest (opens in a new window). Alternatively you can pop into Sportcrest in High Wycombe (opposite Clarks). Branded uniform can only be purchased from Sportscrest, however, the rest of the uniform can be purchased from any shop.
We also have a well stocked second hand uniform shop. Please contact the school office with details of what you are looking for and the size you are looking for. We ask for donations rather than having set prices for second hand uniform.
Hair accessories and Jewellery
Hair accessories should be navy blue or green. Please do not send your child to school wearing jewellery. Plain stud earrings are acceptable but they must be able to be removed by your child or covered for PE and Forest School sessions.
When the weather is cold, the children will need coats, hats, gloves and wellingtons (named and pegged together) in school every day. We will have outdoor activities every day and as the weather changes it is important to have suitable clothing available for your child to wear. Wellingtons are really important, as otherwise we are not able to use the garden, which is such an important part of our learning environment.
Our school is a lovely, 160 year old, Victorian building and can be quite cold on even the hottest days. Please ensure your child brings a cardigan or jumper to school every day.
Please help us by making sure everything is marked with your child’s name!

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care - Ibstone Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
We are proud to offer complete wraparound care. We offer breakfast club (Earlybirds) that runs every morning from 7.45am and we also have a thriving after school club (Kites Club) that runs from the end of the school day until 5.15pm every evening.
Kites Holiday Club has previously run for 4 weeks in the summer holidays, a week at Easter and during October, February and May half term. The demand for Holiday Club is reviewed termly.
We have moved to an online booking system for our wraparound care. Please register and sign in to make a booking:
https://ibstoneceprimaryschool.ipalbookings.com

Key Information
Headteacher's Welcome
Thank you for visiting our school website.
Ibstone CE Primary School is a very small school, situated in an area of outstanding natural beauty which is able to provide a unique learning environment for all children.
We particularly pride ourselves on the fact that our children enjoy school immensely and are valued as unique individuals. Our dedicated staff and Governing Body enthusiastically strive to uphold and develop our provision and we work hard to establish good working relationships with all our parents.
Our aim for the children is to provide a secure learning environment with a Christian ethos where each child is valued, can thrive and achieve their full potential.
Ibstone CE Primary School has a vibrant and caring family ethos. We warmly invite all children and families to participate in and enjoy being part of our special Ibstone community.
I hope that our website will provide an introduction to our school, I look forward to meeting you and showing you around our very special school.
Louise LongHeadteacher

pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Our Vision
Our vision is to nurture our community enabling all to grow through our Christian values. We inspire everyone to be resilient, confident and courageous whilst developing a lasting love of learning.
'Whatever I have, wherever I am, I can make it through anything in the One who makes me who I am.' Philippians 4:13
Our School's Core Christian Values are:
Our school’s vision and its associated values are grounded in a clear theology firmly rooted in a Christian narrative. Our vision is underpinned by our core Christian values. Our values are rooted in biblical teaching and are shared with every member of our school community. Each of us will interpret the words differently but we have developed a definition for staff, parents, governors and children to help explore the meaning of our values at Ibstone. Our vision is lived out through our values. Our values are the tools we use to live out our vision.
These biblical roots are woven throughout our collective worship provision and planning.
We have a range of Bible stories to illustrate our values. These are taken from both the Old and New Testaments and ensure that the teachings of Jesus are explored alongside each value.
Our school is a Church school for everyone and not a faith school for the faithful. You do not need to be a Christian or of any faith to attend this school. Please read our Admissions Policy for further details on admissions to the school. Everyone is welcome at Ibstone!
Ibstone is a Voluntary Aided (VA) Church of England Primary School. A voluntary aided school is a state-funded school in which a foundation or trust (usually a Christian denomination) has substantial influence in the running of the school. Ibstone’s Trust Deed dates from 1852 and included an indenture from the Allnutt and Baker Trust Charity dating from 1742. The school was, ‘opened to all poor persons resident in the parish, of all religions. No child shall be required to learn any catechism or attended Sunday School or place of worship to which his parents or guardians might object’.
Our vision was created by the whole school community. Ibstone has always had a set of values and these have been developed to create our vision and supporting set of values. Children, staff, governors, parents and partners from St Nicholas’ Church and Oxford Diocese were part of the process in agreeing our vision statement and the resources that support this. As a result, our vision is a common, shared aspiration for us all.
Bible stories illustrate our values effectively. In addition to these biblical roots we have a range of stories from other faiths, fables and picture books to support pupils and adults in understanding our Christian values and vision.
You will find more information in our British Values Statement.
